# mtncloud_deployment_file (Resource)

A file of a deployment version whose `type` is `file`, up to 512 MiB. Changing its content uploads it again in place. Files sit at the version's top level: MTN Cloud doesn't list or delete files in folders, so put a folder tree in an archive file (a .zip or .tar.gz) and unpack it on the instance. Destroy deletes the file from the version, not from instances it was deployed to.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mtncloud_deployment_file" "index" {
  deployment_id = mtncloud_deployment.web.id
  version_id    = mtncloud_deployment_version.v2.id
  name          = "index.html"
  content       = "<h1>Hello from MTN Cloud</h1>"
}

# A folder tree goes up as one archive, unpacked on the instance.
resource "mtncloud_deployment_file" "site" {
  deployment_id = mtncloud_deployment.web.id
  version_id    = mtncloud_deployment_version.v2.id
  name          = "site.tar.gz"
  source        = "${path.module}/build/site.tar.gz"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `deployment_id` (String) The deployment, for example `mtncloud_deployment.web.id`.
- `name` (String) The file's name, for example `index.html`. Changing it deletes this file and uploads one with the new name.
- `version_id` (String) The version, for example `mtncloud_deployment_version.v1.id`. Changing it uploads the file to that version.

### Optional

- `content` (String) The content, as text. Set one of `content`, `content_base64` and `source`.
- `content_base64` (String) The content, base64-encoded, for binary data.
- `source` (String) A local file to upload. Its content is compared at every plan, so editing the file uploads it again. A file made later in the same apply is read then.

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) The SHA-256 of the content Terraform uploaded, in hex. Empty after an import, so the next apply uploads the configuration's content.
- `id` (String) `<deployment_id>/<version_id>/<name>`.
- `size_bytes` (Number) The file's size in bytes. When it changes outside Terraform, the next apply uploads the file again.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The deployment's ID, the version's ID and the file's name. The next apply uploads the
# configuration's content.
terraform import mtncloud_deployment_file.index <deployment_id>/<version_id>/index.html
```
